newsitem.title: FRANCE: De Silguy says EMU delay legally impossible.
newsitem.headline: De Silguy says EMU delay legally impossible.

text.p: European Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said on Thursday that any delay to European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) would be legally impossible and would require a change to the Maastricht treaty.

In a speech to French farmers in Toulouse, southern France, he also said that the move towards launching a single currency in 1999 was now irreversible and no politician was seriously considering a delay.

"Delay would be legally impossible -- the treaty states clearly that 'the third phase begins on January 1, 1999'. To change the date, you have to change the treaty," de Silguy, who is responsible for economic and monetary affairs, said.
Economic convergence between countries in Europe was progressing, helped by an acceleration in growth, and budget deficits were being reduced, he said.
Administrations, banks and companies were stepping up their technical preparations.
"The process leading to Economic and Monetary Union is therefore irreversible today. A significant number of member states will be ready at the appropriate time.

"All speculation about an eventual delay to the timetable which one hears frequently at the moment, notably in France, is both useless and unneccessary. There is moreover not one single politician who is considering it seriously," he said.
